conviction_note: The two largest ad-network counterparties, AppLovin and Unity, both reported Q3 2026 well above their own guides after JOYY last spoke. That is a small, positive proxy for BIGO Ads (about 23% of revenue), set against a Q2 beat-and-raise the stock barely paid for (about +0.4% to +1.8%), a decelerating Audience Network and known gross-margin dilution. Hence p_up 56 on abs_move 7.5. The findings sum to +1.1 and the scaled number is +0.9; they agree in sign and are close in size.
bar: Company Q3 2026 revenue guide $602-622M (midpoint $612M, +11.4% to +15.2% YoY), from the Q2 2026 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15505960542266368, 2026-08-25). Segment guide: social entertainment moderate single-digit YoY, BIGO Ads strong double-digit, Shopline mid-20s%. FY26 non-GAAP operating income growth raised to about 20%. Sell-side consensus is disputed. Revenue: $608.2M and non-GAAP EPS $1.39 (Zacks-style preview, https://finviz.com/news/420778/joyys-q3-test-can-revenue-acceleration-outrun-margin-dilution-and-fx-drag, 2026-11-10; whisper $1.42) against $624.44M and EPS $1.42 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/JOYY/estimates). So the revenue bar is anchored to the company guide, and the EPS bar is uncertain by about 3%.
positioning_check: Short interest is low and no squeeze risk is visible. About 1.1M shares short, 2.8 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/joyy/short-interest/). About 2.1% of float, 3.2 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/joyy/short-interest, around 2026-10-05). Baseline skew is -15.27 vol points (25d put IV below call IV, upside paid) and put/call OI is 0.19, but the ATM spread is 137% of mid, so the chain is unreliable as a directional statement. Tape: spot $78.65, -2.43% over 5d, -6.99% over 20d, 7.4% below the 52w high, 44.5% above the 52w low. The stock was $80.96 on 2026-11-10 and up about 37% YTD in October, so it has given back a little into the print.

findings.finding: AppLovin, the largest mobile-gaming ad network (BIGO Ads ranks No.7 globally in Android gaming per AppsFlyer 2026), reported Q3 2026 revenue of about $2.18B (+55% YoY) on 2026-11-04. That beat its own $2.055-2.085B guide by about $100M and points to strong Q3 mobile-gaming ad demand. It speaks to BIGO Ads (Q2: $133.7M, +53% YoY; Audience Network +74%), which JOYY guided only as 'strong double-digit' growth for Q3. It supports total revenue in the upper half of the $602-622M guide rather than at the $608M consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BIGO Ads growth has been the headline on the best reactions. Q3 2025 (BIGO Ads +33%, revenue $540M vs $532M est) rose about 12% on 2025-11-20 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1177307945). Q2 2026 (BIGO Ads +53%, guide above consensus) was roughly flat to +1.8%. The line has paid, but less recently.
findings.why_not_priced: JOYY's consensus ($608.2M) sits in the lower half of a guide set in August, before AppLovin and Unity reported. If the market had carried the peer beat across, consensus would sit near or above the $612M midpoint (one source, Chartmill at $624M, does), and the stock would not have drifted -7% over 20 days into the print. It is a proxy, though: BIGO is a far smaller network and its demand mix is not AppLovin's.
findings.independence: Unity Q3 2026: Grow Solutions $457M (+44%), strategic Grow +90% to $431.5M, above its own guide of up to $385M (https://mobilegamer.biz/unity-posts-first-profit-since-its-ipo-as-vector-grows-126/). That is a different company and document, but the same industry-demand signal.

findings.finding: Unity shut down the ironSource Ads network in Q2 2026 (announced March), per its Q3 2026 release on 2026-11-05. A third-party mobile ad network has left the market, which can free supply and advertiser budget for other networks such as BIGO Audience Network in Q3. Most of the share likely went to Unity Vector (+126% YoY) and AppLovin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print isolates competitor exits. Audience Network growth was 83%, 79% and 74% over the last three quarters (finviz preview), so the market watches this line for deceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: No JOYY preview mentions the ironSource exit. The preview frames Audience Network as decelerating on a big base, which would not be the framing if a share-gain tailwind were assumed. It is an inference with no company confirmation, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: This shares the Unity document with the independence line of finding 1. The fact is different (a competitor exit, not demand), so it is not merged. AppLovin's beat (https://stockanalysis.com/news/applovin-q3-2026-earnings/) is consistent with strong network demand.

findings.finding: Margin quality is the known bear line. Group gross margin was 34.1% in Q2 (down from the mid-35s). BIGO Ads and Shopline gross margins fell QoQ on the mix of lower-margin third-party ads, payments and marketing services. Audience Network growth decelerated 83%, 79%, 74% over three quarters, and the preview flags that margins slipping faster than sales would pause the rerating.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 beat came with flat gross margin and a raised FY operating income guide, and was met with about a flat reaction (+0.4% to +1.8%, https://www.webull.com/news/15505960542266368 context, and search snippets). The beat was not rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: This is largely priced: it is in the wire preview. It is filed as the offset to findings 1-2, because a revenue beat driven by the third-party mix carries the dilution with it. Management already guided operating income to about 20% growth for the year.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 call states the QoQ gross margin declines in BIGO Ads and Shopline on mix (https://www.webull.com/news/15505960542266368).

findings.finding: Management guided a Q3 unrealized FX loss similar to Q2's $14M (Q2 non-GAAP NI $63M vs $77M ex-FX) on a weaker US dollar. But the DXY rose about 1.5-2% in September 2026 to near 102 and was roughly flat over Q3. The FX loss behind the $1.39 EPS consensus may therefore come in smaller than guided, giving non-GAAP net income and EPS upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 the FX loss coincided with an EPS headline 'miss' ($1.24 vs $1.28 in one source) and a flat reaction. That suggests the headline EPS line matters to the initial tape even though the item is non-operating.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide was 'similar trend', and the consensus EPS barely moved, so analysts likely kept the loss in. But JOYY's currency exposure (RMB, SGD and other balances) is not disclosed here, so the sign is uncertain. It is non-operating, with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: DXY path: https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/currency/news/588965 and the J. Safra Sarasin note (https://rankiapro.com/en/insights/j-safra-sarasin-us-growth-outperformance-dollar/), which puts the DXY rising from 99 to about 102 in September. A different source from the company call.

findings.finding: Capital return is live and large: a $1.5B shareholder return program through 2028 and an up-to-$600M buyback authorized in May 2026, of which only $128M was used by 2026-08-21 ($216M of buybacks and $142M of dividends year to date). Management said the share price 'does not fully reflect' the growth. A Q3 buyback-pace update and a dividend declaration at this print are likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (released 2026-05-25/26), when the $1.5B return plan was announced, rose about 12% pre-market, about 12.65% intraday, and over 20% by one headline (https://www.itiger.com/news/1174121061).
findings.why_not_priced: The program itself is priced. What is not known is the Q3 repurchase pace: about $470M remains on the $600M authorization. Execution at around $75-80 is a modest support. This is a continuation, not new news, so it is small.
findings.independence: The finviz 2026-11-10 preview cites $359M repurchased and returned through mid-year (https://finviz.com/news/420778/joyys-q3-test-can-revenue-acceleration-outrun-margin-dilution-and-fx-drag). It rests on the same company disclosure.

findings.finding: Reaction function: the last beat-and-raise was not paid. Q2 2026 brought revenue +16.3%, BIGO Ads +53%, a Q3 guide above consensus and FY operating income raised to about 20%, and the stock moved only about +0.4% to +1.8%. The stock then rose to $80.96 by 2026-11-10 (+6.3% since that report) and has since slipped to $78.65. A good quarter has to beat a higher, partly priced bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 about +12%; Q1 2026 about +12% to +20%; Q2 2026 about flat. Reactions have been large and positive except the last one, which came after a strong run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. It is filed so the panel sees the damped reaction to the last good quarter and the -7% 20-day drift into the print.
findings.independence: The Q2 reaction snippets come from search summaries of webull and stock-track pieces; one result put it at $75.27, +0.36%, on the day of publication.

baseline_tension: The modest positive lean agrees with the baseline's upside-paid skew (-15 vol points), but that chain is too wide to trust. It cuts slightly against the -7% 20-day drift, and the flat reaction to the last beat-and-raise argues for keeping p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1/6 (reaction function; finding inside the guided range): the peer-demand proxies land inside the 'strong double-digit' BIGO Ads guide, and the last beat-and-raise was not paid. Finding 1 cut from 1.0 to 0.8, finding 2 from 0.5 to 0.4, and p_up from 57 to 56.
Rule 2 (one-offs): the FX item is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it was cut from 0.3 to 0.2.

Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): BIGO Ads is about 23% of revenue, and the proxies say nothing about social entertainment (about 70%, guided moderate single digits). The cut was taken in the sizes above, not again.
Rule 6 (bar): consensus is disputed ($608M vs $624M), but the company guide gives a sourced revenue bar, so no cap; the EPS-sensitive FX finding stays small.
